items.narrative: Password hashing algorithm decision revised. Bcrypt was selected at 4:03pm but is now being replaced with Argon2id. The driver for this change is Argon2id's superior resistance to GPU-accelerated attacks compared to Bcrypt. Argon2id uses both time and memory costs in its key derivation function, making it fundamentally harder to parallelize on GPUs than Bcrypt's iterative-only approach.
items.facts: ["Argon2id selected as password hashing algorithm","Replaces Bcrypt decision made at 4:03pm on Sep 23, 2026","Rationale: Argon2id provides better resistance to GPU-accelerated attacks","Argon2id is memory-hard, making GPU parallelization significantly more difficult"]

items.title: Bcrypt selected for password hashing
items.subtitle: Bcrypt adopted as the password hashing standard for authentication layer
items.narrative: Following earlier architectural decisions on compression and cache eviction strategies, the system design now specifies bcrypt for password hashing. This selection aligns with industry best practices and ensures the authentication layer uses a mature, well-supported cryptographic standard for securing user passwords.
items.facts: ["Bcrypt chosen for password hashing implementation","Selection rationale: industry standard and well-maintained library","Addresses security requirements for credential storage"]

items.title: Cache eviction strategy switched from LFU to LRU with 300-second TTL
items.subtitle: Replaced LFU eviction with LRU eviction and added 300-second TTL for simplified cache reasoning.
items.narrative: The cache layer eviction strategy was switched from LFU (Least Frequently Used) to LRU (Least Recently Used) with a 300-second TTL. LRU is a simpler eviction model that only tracks recency of access, making behavior more predictable and easier to reason about compared to LFU, which tracks access frequency and is more complex to understand and debug.
items.facts: ["Previous cache layer used LFU (Least Frequently Used) eviction strategy","New cache layer uses LRU (Least Recently Used) eviction strategy","Cache entries configured with 300-second time-to-live (TTL)","Rationale for change: LRU is simpler to reason about than LFU"]

items.title: LFU eviction selected for cache layer
items.subtitle: LFU eviction policy chosen based on observed access patterns in cache usage
items.narrative: The team selected LFU (Least Frequently Used) as the eviction policy for their cache layer. This decision is grounded in analysis of actual access patterns observed in the system, indicating that a frequency-based approach aligns with how data is being accessed. LFU eviction removes items that are accessed least frequently when the cache reaches capacity, preserving hot items that are accessed more often.
items.facts: ["LFU (Least Frequently Used) eviction policy selected for cache layer","Decision justified by observed access patterns in the system","Eviction strategy for managing cache capacity and retention"]

items.title: Zstd selected over gzip for compression layer
items.subtitle: Switched compression algorithm to zstd for superior ratio and performance characteristics
items.narrative: The compression layer algorithm selection was revised from gzip to zstd. This decision prioritizes compression ratio efficiency while maintaining acceptable performance characteristics. Zstd offers superior compression density compared to gzip, which reduces storage and transmission costs without sacrificing throughput in the application's performance envelope.
items.facts: ["Compression algorithm changed from gzip to zstd","Decision rationale: zstd provides better compression ratio than gzip","Zstd performance metrics meet or exceed gzip in the target workload"]

items.title: Gzip selected for compression layer
items.subtitle: Gzip chosen for production compression due to proven reliability and broad tooling support
items.narrative: The project team decided to use gzip for the compression layer rather than exploring newer or alternative compression formats. The decision prioritizes stability and tooling maturity over potential performance gains from newer algorithms. Gzip's broad ecosystem support and proven track record in production systems make it suitable for this component.
items.facts: ["Gzip chosen as the compression algorithm for the project's compression layer","Decision rationale: well-tested algorithm with mature, widely-available tooling","Indicates production-grade compression implementation, not experimental approach"]
